items.followUp: What is the role of an enzyme in a chemical reaction?

rubric.why: The active site binds the specific substrate.
rubric.description: Identifies the active site as the place where the substrate binds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the substrate binds or fits at the active site.

rubric.why: The active site enables the enzyme to catalyse the reaction.
rubric.description: States that the active site helps convert the substrate into product.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the catalytic role or formation of product.

modelAnswer: The active site is the specific region of an enzyme to which its substrate binds.
It enables the enzyme to catalyse the reaction and convert the substrate into product.

items.followUp: Who coined the term cell, and in what year?

rubric.why: The scientist who introduced the term was Kühne.
rubric.description: Names Kühne.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Kühne.

rubric.why: The term enzyme was used in 1878.
rubric.description: Gives the year.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct year.

modelAnswer: Wilhelm Kühne used the term enzyme in 1878.

items.followUp: What is the approximate length of the human small intestine?

rubric.why: The human oesophagus is approximately 25 centimetres long.
rubric.description: Gives the approximate length.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the value 25.

rubric.why: The length is expressed in centimetres.
rubric.description: Gives the correct unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the unit centimetres.

modelAnswer: The human oesophagus is about 25 cm long.

items.followUp: Differentiate between saturated and unsaturated fatty acids by their bonds.

rubric.why: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon–carbon double bonds.
rubric.description: States the defining bond feature of saturated fatty acids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they have no double bonds or only single bonds.

rubric.why: Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon–carbon double bonds.
rubric.description: States the defining bond feature of unsaturated fatty acids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they have one or more double bonds.

modelAnswer: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon–carbon double bonds.
Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon–carbon double bonds.

items.followUp: What is the function of thrombocytes in blood?

rubric.why: Thrombocytes are blood platelets, which are cell fragments.
rubric.description: Identifies thrombocytes as platelets or cell fragments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either identification.

rubric.why: Thrombocytes help blood to clot.
rubric.description: States their role in clotting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning blood clotting or clot formation.

modelAnswer: Thrombocytes are platelets, or cell fragments, present in the blood.
They help in blood clotting.

items.followUp: What are the three types of cellular organization found in organisms?

rubric.why: Cellular organization describes how cells are arranged in an organism.
rubric.description: Defines cellular organization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it is the arrangement or organization of cells.

rubric.why: A unicellular organism consists of one cell.
rubric.description: Names and explains the unicellular type.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying unicellular organization as consisting of one cell.

rubric.why: In colonial organization, similar cells live together in a colony.
rubric.description: Names and explains the colonial type.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying colonial organization as cells living together in a colony.

rubric.why: A multicellular organism consists of many cells.
rubric.description: Names and explains the multicellular type.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying multicellular organization as consisting of many cells.

modelAnswer: Cellular organization is the arrangement of cells in an organism.
In unicellular organization, an organism consists of a single cell.
In colonial organization, similar cells live together in a colony.
In multicellular organization, an organism consists of many cells.

items.followUp: Name the three types of plastids and state one function of each.

rubric.why: Plastids are organelles found in plant cells.
rubric.description: Identifies plastids as organelles of plant cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that plastids are organelles found in plant cells.

rubric.why: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Gives the chloroplast type and its function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking chloroplasts with photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to flowers and fruits.
rubric.description: Gives the chromoplast type and its role in colour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking chromoplasts with colour or pigments.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids involved in storing food.
rubric.description: Gives the leucoplast type and its storage role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking leucoplasts with storage.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts store food materials such as starch, oils or proteins.
rubric.description: Names a stored food material.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming starch, oil or protein as a stored material.

modelAnswer: Plastids are organelles found in plant cells.
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to flowers and fruits.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
Leucoplasts may store starch, oils or proteins.

items.followUp: State the rules for writing the scientific name of an organism using binomial nomenclature.

rubric.why: A scientific name consists of two words: the genus name and the species name.
rubric.description: States that the name has two parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the two names as genus and species.

rubric.why: The first word is the genus name.
rubric.description: Identifies the first part of the name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the first word is the genus.

rubric.why: The second word is the species name.
rubric.description: Identifies the second part of the name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the second word is the species.

rubric.why: Scientific names are written in italics or underlined when handwritten; Homo sapiens is an example.
rubric.description: Gives a correct writing convention or example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the italic/underline convention or giving a correct binomial example.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature is the system of naming organisms with two words.
The first word is the genus name and begins with a capital letter.
The second word is the species name and begins with a small letter.
The two words are written in italics, or underlined separately when handwritten; for example, Homo sapiens.
